title: Contributing
description: Learn by doing, on The Labs itself. Anyone can contribute; every step up means you've worked hands-on in more of how The Labs runs.
draft: A working draft. The board hasn't approved the levels or the workstreams yet, and the pins are still being made.

title: Build
The Labs
hero.lede: The Labs teaches by doing, and that includes running The Labs. Every step up means you've had your hands on more of how it works.
hero.status: First pins: our two steering committees
hero.pinAlt: The Contributing Member pin, turning to follow your pointer

start.title: Some people use the playbook. Some people write the next page.
start.lede: The Labs is built by the people in it. Pick a way in.

items.label: Contribute
items.title: Make something better.
items.body: A playbook, a flyer, a kit, a line of code. Anyone can suggest a change, and you're credited by name.

items.label: Take a role
items.title: Do it in public.
items.body: Upskiller, Poderator, Mentor, Ambassador. Get trained, then practise until the role's lead says you've got it. Ambassador is open now.

items.label: Get recognized
items.title: Earn the pin.
items.body: When The Labs runs on something you made, the people who saw it put your name forward. That's your first pin.

rings.title: Every step up is more of The Labs, hands on.
rings.lede: Each level means you've worked in more of The Labs' workstreams: the major ones, and the minor ones along the way. The pin marks how far you've gone.

steps.line: You made something The Labs now runs on.
steps.how: Hands-on in one workstream, with work The Labs now runs on. A line on the register says what it was.

steps.line: You've done it, so you can review it.
steps.how: Practised in two major workstreams, sponsored by two pin holders from different workstreams or Labs.
steps.trusted: Reviewing work, and new Practitioners, in the workstreams you know.

steps.line: You've worked in every part of The Labs.
steps.how: Hands-on in every major workstream, and some of the minor ones.
steps.trusted: Approving changes to your Lab's playbooks, within a written grant from the board.

steps.line: You know how all of it fits together.
steps.how: Hands-on across the major and minor workstreams. Nominated by Maintainers, confirmed by the board.
steps.trusted: Setting the direction for a workstream. The board keeps the final say.

rings.names: Major workstreams (draft): Build Cycle, Learning Pathways, Community & Outreach, Platform (OLOS), Operations & Governance. Minor ones include events, communications and research. Workstreams and level names are drafts until the board decides. [PLACEHOLDER]

metal.title: Every level has its own pin.
metal.lede: Pick a level and turn its pin. Each is given in person, and none is ever for sale.
metal.stageLabel: The {rank} pin. Drag, or use the arrow keys, to turn it.

given.title: It starts with the work. It ends with a handshake.

steps.title: Do the work.
steps.body: Get hands-on: make something The Labs can reuse, or practise in the workstreams a level asks for.

steps.title: Someone vouches.
steps.body: Pin holders put your name forward. For the next level, that's two sponsors, from different workstreams or Labs.

steps.title: It's recorded.
steps.body: Your Lab checks it, and HQ writes it on the register with a line on what you did.

steps.title: Pinned.
steps.body: At the next regional gathering. Your sponsors pin it on and say a sentence about why.

status.title: Every level is active or emeritus.
status.lede: Your level is yours for good. What changes is whether you're doing the work right now.

items.label: Active
items.title: Doing the work now.
items.body: You hold a seat in your Lab, with the permissions your level brings. The board grants them in writing, and the register shows who's active.

items.label: Emeritus
items.title: Stepped back, still yours.
items.body: You keep the level, the title, the pin, and your voice. Come back to any open seat without starting over.

decides.title: Levels recognize. Boards decide.
rules: Levels carry no vote. The boards run programs, money, people and the brand.
No one can buy a pin, a level, or a vote.
It's recognition, not certification. It's the community saying thank you.
The one exception to keeping your level: a serious breach of the Code of Conduct.

join.title: Every pin starts with one contribution.
join.lede: The way in today is the ambassador program. Tell your story, bring someone to their first workshop, and see what you end up building.

footer.renders: Images of the pin are 3D renders, not photos. The real pins are still being made.
